neighbours.label: The -where indefinite place adverbs: ' somewhere', ' anywhere', ' elsewhere', ' everywhere' (and weaker ' wherever'), in any context
fire: We were hoping to find somewhere quiet to eat dinner after the long drive.
I know I left my keys somewhere in the kitchen, but I cannot find them.
You won't get service like this anywhere else in town, trust me.
The old map suggested that the treasure was buried somewhere near the river.
If the store is closed, you might try looking elsewhere for a replacement part.
After the storm, broken branches were lying everywhere across the park.
She said she would follow him anywhere, even across the ocean.
Somebody somewhere must have a copy of that rare recording.
quiet: After the long drive, our family picked a quiet restaurant for dinner.
My keys were on the kitchen counter the whole time, right next to the bread.
The service at this shop is better than at the other one in town.
According to the old map, the treasure was buried near the river bend.
When that shop closes, try the hardware store across the street.
Once the wind died down, broken branches covered the lawns of the park.
Where did you put the blanket that was on the couch yesterday?
One of the archivists must have a copy of that rare recording.

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
